item.title: Furofushi Onsen: Aomori's Seaside Sunset Bath — Guide
item.description: Furofushi Onsen is a famed seaside hot spring in Fukaura where you soak in amber-coloured open-air baths at the very edge of the Sea of Japan, facing the sunset. Iron-rich water turns golden-brown on contact with the air, and waves break just metres away — a bucket-list bathing experience on the Gono Line coast. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Fukaura, Aomori Hours Day bathing ~8:00–16:00 (varies) Admission Day bath ~¥600 Time needed 1–1.

item.title: Senjojiki Coast: Aomori's Sunset Rock Shelf — Guide
item.description: The Senjojiki Coast at Fukaura is a broad, flat shelf of pale volcanic rock, thrust up from the sea by an earthquake in 1792. A celebrated stop on the scenic Gono Line, it’s known for spectacular Sea of Japan sunsets and easy shoreline strolling over the tabletop rocks. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Fukaura, Aomori Hours Always open (sunset best) Admission Free Time needed About 1 hour Best time Summer & autumn; sunset any clear day What to See The wide flat rock shelf uplifted in 1792.

item.title: Enoshima Guide: Shrine, Sea Candle & Sunset (Kanagawa)
item.description: A small sacred island linked to the Shonan coast by a bridge, Enoshima is one of the most beloved escapes near Tokyo — a hill of shrines, caves, gardens and sea views topped by a lighthouse-like observation tower. Climb (or ride the outdoor escalators) past the Enoshima Shrine to the Sea Candle, whose deck delivers superb panoramas over Sagami Bay to Mt. Fuji, gorgeous at sunset. Below, the wave-carved Iwaya caves and a lively lane of seafood and grilled-octopus stalls make it a perfect half-day, easily paired with the Shonan beaches.

item.title: Umeda Sky Building Guide: The Floating Garden Observatory
item.description: One of Osaka’s boldest pieces of architecture, the Umeda Sky Building is two 40-storey towers joined at the top by a doughnut-shaped Floating Garden Observatory seemingly suspended in mid-air. Glass escalators cross the open void between the towers to reach the rooftop, where an open-air deck gives a 360-degree panorama over the whole of Osaka — spectacular at sunset and after dark. Frequently listed among the world’s great buildings, it’s the city’s best skyline viewpoint and an experience in itself.
